questions.question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of Shadow DOM?

options.text: To provide style and markup encapsulation (scoping) for a component
To store component state in a database

questions.explanation: Shadow DOM creates a scoped subtree so internal styles/markup don't leak out and page styles don't bleed in — the basis of Web Components.

questions.question: What is the 'shadow host'?

options.text: The regular DOM element that a shadow root is attached to

questions.explanation: The shadow host is the ordinary element (e.g. <my-element>) to which a shadow root is attached, becoming the container for the shadow tree.

questions.question: Which CSS selector targets the shadow HOST from inside the shadow tree?
questions.explanation: :host selects the host element from within the shadow DOM. ::slotted() targets light-DOM children projected via <slot>.

questions.question: How are child elements passed from the light DOM into a shadow tree?
questions.explanation: <slot> elements in the shadow tree define where and how light-DOM children are distributed (composed) into the shadow content.

questions.question: What is 'event retargeting' in Shadow DOM?

options.text: Events crossing the shadow boundary are reported with the nearest non-shadow ancestor as target

questions.explanation: To preserve encapsulation, when an event crosses out of a shadow tree, its target is retargeted to the shadow host rather than internal nodes.

questions.question: In Angular, View Encapsulation uses Shadow DOM style scoping. Which mode uses the real Shadow DOM?
questions.explanation: ViewEncapsulation.ShadowDom attaches a real shadow root. The default Emulated fakes scoping with attribute selectors for broader support.

questions.question: Why might you choose 'open' shadow mode over 'closed'?

options.text: Open exposes shadowRoot for testing/tooling; closed hides it and breaks testability

questions.explanation: Open mode lets element.shadowRoot be accessed (tests, devtools, libraries). Closed mode hides it, hurting testability with little real security gain.

questions.question: Do CSS selectors from the main document reach INSIDE a shadow root?

options.text: No — styles inside don't leak out and outside selectors can't reach in (unless ::part/::slotted)

questions.explanation: Shadow DOM enforces style scoping: internal styles stay in, external selectors stay out. ::part() and ::slotted() are the sanctioned bridges.
